description: The Energy Demand Research Project was a major set of trials in Great Britain testing how households respond over the long term to better information about their energy use, including smart-type meters. Energy suppliers ran the trials, mostly from late 2007 or early 2008 to the end of 2010, combining different measures and covering about 60,000 households, some 18,000 of them with smart-type meters; AECOM Building Engineering deposited the data, which the UK Data Service released in 2018. The anonymised sample in this release includes just over 14,000 households with their energy consumption readings and trial information. Coverage: households across Great Britain in the trial groups. Access: download from the UK Data Service. Licence: the data are safeguarded and available to registered users under the End User Licence Agreement; free. Caveats: trial participants are not a random national sample, and the data predate the national smart meter roll-out. Simulation uses are residential load profiles and behavioural response to feedback in demand and flexibility models. Related records: the Energy Follow Up Survey 2011 and RECS.
